title: I kept working on my bike game — now it has a story mode, upgrades, jumps and radio
author: Bottle_777
selftext:
A few days ago I posted my little browser bike game here and got a ton of feedback — both positive and brutal, haha.

So I kept working on it.

It now has a story mode, bike progression and upgrades, new obstacles, jumping, improved visuals, and even an AI-generated radio.

The funny part is that I still have basically zero programming knowledge and haven’t manually written the code. My whole workflow is still describing what I want, testing it, finding what feels wrong, and repeatedly directing the AI until it works the way I want.

At this point it feels much closer to an actual small game than the original endless-road prototype.

I’m especially curious whether the progression and story mode make it something you’d actually want to keep playing.

Playable Link: [https://royal-waterfall-a15e.quietforge.workers.dev/](https://royal-waterfall-a15e.quietforge.workers.dev/)

comments.author: No_Age4655
comments.body: Nice, I like the crash mechanics

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: Glad you liked it! I spent a lot of time working on it.

replies.author: No_Age4655
replies.body: Keep on going, maybe work on the player model a bit, the bike looks great. You got something good going

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: I agree, the player and NPC models look pretty primitive. I could probably get a better result by tweaking them manually, but I intentionally made everything through AI prompts as a kind of challenge. It clearly has no idea what humans are supposed to look like, haha.

replies.author: No_Age4655
replies.body: Yeah I personally struggle getting 3d games to look how its supposed to, maybe try a free to use model

comments.author: FratKing2025
comments.body: very nice, I think if you made the HUD look more game like and less AI look, it would look better

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
Yeah, it definitely has that slightly overdone AI-futuristic flavor in the HUD right now.

Beyond that, I’ve been thinking about pushing the game more toward a pixel-art / retro console style overall — I think that would help smooth out some of the visual quirks, and I personally love that aesthetic.

I could probably even add a visual style switcher so people can choose whatever vibe they prefer.

comments.author: TriggerHydrant
comments.body: Fuck yeah glad you kept going! Also if you need some (free) music [feel free to get in touch!](https://thomasgeelens.com/#pop)

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: Oh, that’s a great selection — thanks, I’ll definitely keep it in mind! When I was making the game, I somehow never even thought about using free tracks. For some reason I was looking for existing radio stations I could just hook into, couldn’t find anything suitable, and ended up generating some simple instrumental music instead, haha.

replies.author: TriggerHydrant
replies.body: That makes sense! And sure get in touch either here or using my website, I’ve started to offer tunes for fellow developers since I’ve got a huge discography and think that a lot of the tunes would fit well for a wide variety of games. All the best with the game and let me know!

comments.author: TheFish77
comments.body: I dig it. I feel like the levels should get increasingly outlandish. Like one where you're on a volcano with dinosaurs and an undersea level with sharks and giant squid.

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
That’s a really good idea — more craziness is always better. I actually played with that a little during development by trying to make a high-speed downhill section on a snowy mountain, but I decided to put it aside so I could finish the core game first.

I like your ideas even more, though!

replies.author: TheFish77
replies.body: Oh I like the snow level idea too. A snowman or penguin randomly getting in the way 🤔

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: No, mostly Codex — Luna Extra High / Max, and occasionally Sol.

comments.author: Objective-Wasabi9970
comments.body: Looks great! What was your graphic assets workflow?

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
Thanks! I didn’t make anything manually or use any premade assets. I basically just looked at what the AI produced and kept asking it to adjust the colors, shapes, and placement. A lot of the time I had to describe pretty precisely what each element should look like and how it should be positioned.

Sometimes it was actually pretty hard to communicate exactly which detail I wanted changed, so for that I vibe-coded a little in-game asset viewer and clicked on specific elements so I could refer to them more clearly in my prompts.

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body: Have you done any memory optimization? It's got some serious load lag on my machine and I have an 8 core processor and 4GB Nvidia card.

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body: Yeah, I fixed a bunch of performance issues I found before release, but I’m sure there are still some left. I’ll keep improving the optimization in future updates.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: I think the concept is great, game play needs focused on. It looks a bit rough to play just from the gameplay video alone, I think youve got something that can be monetized if cleaned up, no clue what retention look like or designed for wise but could definitely be a mobile game worse case scenario

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
Yeah, there’s definitely still a lot that could be improved. And I definitely wouldn’t want to turn it into some mobile F2P cash-grab.

I like the idea of optional donations from players much more. If nobody pays, then hey — at least they had a good time, and I had fun making the game. In the end, I think that’s what matters most.

comments.author: CybuhDasher
comments.body: i played the game the first time you posted and somehow the controls are even worse than before lol. and the game is still too easy.

replies.author: Bottle_777
replies.body:
Haha, yeah, you can get pretty good at it pretty quickly. I still haven’t fully decided whether the game should be more challenging or more relaxing.

Either way, I’m curious — were you playing with the PC controls or on mobile?

comments.author: drtreadwater
comments.body: I love the tornado, i bet that felt like a risky addition but it pays off!

comments.author: ASAF12341
comments.body: I like it, but there's so much good GLB for human foes for free. I think this will upgrade your game.
